summary: The starter prompt clearly defines a chargeback-dispute multi-agent Node.js sample using LangChain with an orchestrator + three agents and an end-to-end flow. The run environment (Node.js 24, a reachable DocumentDB cluster, and DATABASE name sample_fintech_18) is provided in the accompanying skill_md and multiple installed skills cover DocumentDB best practices (driver singleton, connection guidance, indexing, vector search, etc.). Several important engineering details are left unspecified (driver version, collection/document schema, AI model/provider, API surface, seed data and indexing parameters, README/tests), so a builder will fill these with reasonable defaults (Express API, mongodb npm driver latest 5.x, OpenAI models via env vars, small idempotent seed script, single MongoClient singleton).

rubric.found_in_prompt: build a Node.js LangChain multi-agent system where an orchestrator receives a chargeback claim, delegates to an evidence-gathering agent ... policy-reasoning agent ... decision agent that writes the accept/reject outcome back to DocumentDB.
rubric.note: Business problem and what the sample demonstrates are clearly stated.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Node.js LangChain multi-agent system ... orchestrator, evidence-gathering agent, policy-reasoning agent, decision agent
rubric.note: Multi-agent orchestration with LangChain is explicitly requested.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Using the DocumentDB skill, build a Node.js LangChain ...
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use Node.js 24 (the run environment states Node.js 24 is available).
rubric.note: Prompt states Node.js; skill_md provides concrete runtime (Node.js 24).

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the official mongodb Node.js driver (npm package 'mongodb') at a current 5.x release that supports MongoDB 7.0; follow documentdb-driver guidance to instantiate a singleton MongoClient.
rubric.note: Starter prompt doesn't name the driver or version. documentdb-driver covers usage patterns (singleton) but not an exact package version.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Using the DocumentDB skill ... write ... back to DocumentDB.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the provided live, vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol) reachable via DOCUMENTDB_URI as described in skill_md.
rubric.note: skill_md explicitly describes the available cluster and forbids creating a different one for the sample.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Connection string is read from env var DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime; other secrets / model keys placed in env vars and not checked into repo.
rubric.note: skill_md instructs to read DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment and to avoid writing secrets into files or README.

rubric.found_in_prompt: evidence-gathering agent that fetches transaction and communication documents from DocumentDB
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a dedicated database named 'sample_fintech_18' (skill_md). Collections assumed: 'transactions', 'communications' (and likely 'claims' or 'decisions'). Documents include claimId/transactionId, timestamps, amounts, message text, and any metadata. Use schemaVersion field and avoid >16MB docs.
rubric.note: Prompt requires fetching transactions & communications but does not specify collection names, field names, or exact document shapes; documentdb-data-modeling can guide choices but doesn't supply concrete schema.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create a small idempotent seed script that upserts a handful of transactions, communications and a sample claim (e.g., using claimId) into 'sample_fintech_18'. The seed script will check for existing docs or upsert to allow re-run without duplication.
rubric.note: Starter prompt doesn't include sample data or how to load it; reference requirements expect a seed script but it's not specified here.

rubric.found_in_prompt: fetches transaction and communication documents ... associated with the provided claim identifier
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement simple queries that filter by claimId or transactionId. Create single-field indexes on claimId/transactionId. No vector or full-text index is strictly required unless the policy or evidence agent needs semantic search; if embeddings are used, create a vector index sized to the chosen embedding dims.
rubric.note: Specific index shapes and parameters are not specified; documentdb-indexing can guide decisions but the builder must choose index keys and parameters.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use LangChain Node.js with an LLM provider via env vars (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY). For embeddings, assume OpenAI text-embedding-3-small and for reasoning use an LLM like gpt-4o-mini or a similar hosted model. Embedding dimension assumed to match the chosen model (e.g., 1536 dims for text-embedding-3-small).
rubric.note: No embedding model or chat model/provider is named in the prompt; that materially affects index dimensions and call sites.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement a minimal HTTP API (Express) with POST /claims/submit or POST /claims/:id/decide which accepts a claim payload or claimId and triggers the orchestrator. Include simple JSON responses and a /health endpoint.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't specify CLI vs API vs UI; an API is the most likely and practical choice for demonstration.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision a cluster. Use the existing DocumentDB cluster described in the run environment. If infrastructure-as-code is required, use documentdb-azure-deployment skill, but the run instructions currently forbid creating another cluster.
rubric.note: skill_md explicitly states the cluster is already provisioned and should be used for verification.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide README with commands: npm install, cp .env.example .env (fill vars), npm run seed, npm start; tests via npm test (Jest) with unit tests using mocks so they run without a live cluster.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't include step-by-step run/test instructions; builder must add them.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Define done as: (1) orchestrator accepts a claim and invokes agents in order; (2) evidence agent retrieves docs from DocumentDB; (3) policy agent outputs a recommendation; (4) decision agent writes an accept/reject document back to sample_fintech_18 and the flow is demonstrated in the README and a recorded run.
rubric.note: No acceptance criteria in prompt; builder will need to define them to complete the sample.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Avoid provisioning new clusters or writing secrets to repo. Keep example data small to limit costs. Do not attempt production-grade HA, RBAC or CMK configuration beyond recommended best practices.
rubric.note: Prompt and skill_md impose some constraints (use existing cluster), but cost limits and non-goals are not fully enumerated.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use standard Node layout: package.json, src/, tests/, README.md, .env.example (placeholders only). Use 'Azure DocumentDB' name consistently. Pin dependency versions in package.json (lockfile via package-lock.json).
rubric.note: No explicit repo layout rules are provided; builder will apply common Node.js conventions.

contradictions: The prompt says 'Using the DocumentDB skill' but there is no single installed skill named exactly 'DocumentDB' — instead several DocumentDB-related skills are installed (documentdb-driver, documentdb-connection, etc.). The builder will need to decide which of the installed skills to consult.
questions_for_author: Which AI provider and exact models should be used for embeddings and policy reasoning (this affects vector dimensions, env vars, and index choices)?
Do you want an HTTP API (recommended) or a CLI/other interface for submitting claims and showing results?

Should the sample include an idempotent seed script with sample transactions/communications and exact collection names (if yes, please confirm preferred collection names like 'transactions' and 'communications')?
requirements_at_risk: A `.env.example` lists every setting with placeholder values — not specified in starter prompt or skill_md; builder must add it.
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — embedding model not specified, so index dims are at risk of mismatching.
Vector index parameters chosen for the sample's data size and README explains how to change them — index parameters not provided in prompt; builder will invent defaults, so this is at risk.
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — prompt does not request a seed script; this is likely to be omitted unless builder adds it.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — no search endpoint is specified and error handling for embedding failures is not in the prompt.
Search results include the similarity score — semantic-search behavior is not requested; similarity scoring is at risk of being omitted.

Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt` — Node projects don't use requirements.txt; the equivalent (pinned package.json versions and lockfile) is not specified and may be inconsistent with the reference expectation.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — tests and mocks are not described; builder may not include offline-capable unit tests.

Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — skill_md forbids provisioning in this environment and the starter prompt doesn't request IaC; this requirement is at risk.
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — README is not requested explicitly in the starter prompt and may be incomplete if the builder omits it.
